claims.text: This paper introduces Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO), a reinforcement learning algorithm that defines importance ratios based on sequence likelihood rather than token-level metrics.
GSPO performs sequence-level clipping, rewarding, and optimization, achieving superior training efficiency and performance compared to GRPO.
The algorithm notably stabilizes Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) RL training and has been instrumental in improvements to Qwen3 models.
Improved stability for MoE RL training
Demonstrated superior performance over GRPO
GSPO represents a direct evolution from GRPO, addressing limitations in token-level optimization by operating at the sequence level.
This paper challenges the prevailing view that GRPO's efficacy stems from large group sizes for accurate statistical estimates.
Instead, the authors propose that GRPO's effectiveness arises from its implicit contrastive objective, structurally related to preference learning methods like DPO.
This insight motivates 2-GRPO, a variant using only two rollouts that retains 97.6% of 16-GRPO's performance while requiring only 12.5% of rollouts and 21% of training time.
Theoretical analysis revealing GRPO's contrastive nature
2-GRPO variant with minimal group size
Significant efficiency improvements with maintained performance
Provides fundamental theoretical insights into GRPO's mechanisms and demonstrates that large group sizes are unnecessary.
This work revisits GRPO from a REINFORCE-like algorithm perspective, finding that a simple rejection sampling baseline (RAFT) yields competitive performance.
The main advantage of GRPO arises from discarding prompts with entirely incorrect responses rather than reward normalization.
The authors propose Reinforce-Rej, filtering both entirely incorrect and entirely correct samples, improving KL efficiency and stability.
Critical analysis of GRPO's effectiveness sources
RAFT as a robust baseline
Reinforce-Rej as a lightweight alternative
Questions the necessity of GRPO's complexity and advocates for simpler, more interpretable approaches.
MGRPO addresses inefficient exploration dynamics in standard GRPO by introducing a two-layer architecture.
The first layer generates initial responses, while the second layer identifies and corrects errors, creating a self-correction loop.
This provides implicit process-level supervision without requiring densely-annotated reward models, significantly outperforming standard GRPO on mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
Superior performance on reasoning tasks
Extends GRPO to enable self-correction capabilities, addressing the single-error invalidation problem in complex reasoning chains.
This paper extends GRPO-style training to diffusion models through DiffusionNFT, optimizing directly on the forward process via flow matching.
DiffusionNFT contrasts positive and negative generations, incorporating reinforcement signals into supervised learning.
It achieves up to 25× efficiency improvement over FlowGRPO, eliminates likelihood estimation needs, and works with arbitrary black-box solvers.
Extension of GRPO principles to diffusion models
Forward process optimization via flow matching
Dramatic efficiency improvements (25× over FlowGRPO)
Demonstrates GRPO's applicability beyond language models to diffusion-based generation, addressing intractable likelihood challenges.
SAPO replaces hard clipping with smooth, temperature-controlled gating that adaptively attenuates off-policy updates while preserving useful learning signals.
Unlike GSPO's hard clipping that suppresses all gradients for sequences with off-policy tokens, SAPO selectively down-weights only offending tokens.
Compared to GRPO, SAPO replaces hard token-level clipping with smooth scaling, enabling more informative and stable updates.
Soft gating mechanism replacing hard clipping
Token-adaptive while maintaining sequence coherence
Improved training stability and Pass@1 performance
Addresses GRPO's hard clipping limitations through adaptive, smooth scaling for more stable optimization.
DAPO introduces Decoupled Clip and Dynamic Sampling Policy Optimization, achieving 50 points on AIME 2024 using Qwen2.5-32B base model.

The paper open-sources a complete state-of-the-art RL system with four key techniques, training code built on the verl framework, and curated datasets, addressing the reproducibility challenges in large-scale LLM RL.
Decoupled clip and dynamic sampling techniques
Reproducible results on reasoning benchmarks
Provides open-source infrastructure and techniques that complement GRPO-based approaches for large-scale training.
LUFFY addresses the on-policy limitation of existing RLVR approaches by augmenting training with off-policy reasoning traces.
The framework combines Mixed-Policy GRPO with theoretically guaranteed convergence and policy shaping via regularized importance sampling.
LUFFY achieves +6.4 average gain across six math benchmarks and enables training in scenarios where on-policy RLVR fails completely.
Off-policy guidance integration with GRPO
Significant improvements on math benchmarks
Extends GRPO to incorporate off-policy demonstrations, transcending inherent on-policy limitations.

This paper demonstrates that vanilla PPO with GAE (λ=1, γ=1) and rule-based rewards, without KL regularization, is sufficient to scale up reasoning performance, replicating DeepSeek-R1-Zero scaling phenomena.
The approach achieves superior performance across AIME2024, MATH500, and GPQA Diamond with only 1/10 of DeepSeek-R1-Zero's training steps.
Minimalist RL approach matching state-of-the-art
10× efficiency improvement over DeepSeek-R1-Zero
Questions the necessity of complex algorithms like GRPO, showing that simpler approaches can achieve comparable results.
TOPR uses asymmetric, tapered importance sampling for stable learning without KL regularization.
The algorithm handles positive and negative examples in a unified framework with Monte Carlo simplicity.
Experiments show TOPR matches 70B-parameter model performance with 8B models by properly leveraging both positive and negative examples in the off-policy regime.
Tapered importance sampling for stability
Matching larger model performance with smaller models
Provides an alternative approach to GRPO that achieves similar goals through off-policy REINFORCE with tapered sampling.

Wu et al. (2025) fundamentally challenge the assumption that large group sizes are necessary, demonstrating that GRPO's efficacy stems from implicit contrastive learning rather than statistical accuracy.
Xiong et al. (2025) and Hu et al. (2025) further question GRPO's complexity, showing that simpler approaches like rejection sampling and vanilla PPO can achieve competitive or superior results.
Stability Enhancements: Gao et al. (2025) introduce SAPO's soft gating mechanism, replacing hard clipping with adaptive scaling for more stable updates.
Efficiency Improvements: Wu et al. (2025) demonstrate that minimal group sizes suffice, while Ding et al. (2025) show that multi-layer architectures with self-correction improve sample efficiency.
Off-Policy Extensions: Yan et al. (2025) and Le Roux et al. (2025) extend GRPO-related approaches to incorporate off-policy data, addressing fundamental limitations of on-policy training.
Yu et al. (2025) and Hu et al. (2025) provide crucial open-source implementations, addressing reproducibility challenges in large-scale RL training.
